findings.issue: Masculine imperative, but every other addressee in this scene-set is a sester addressed in the feminine (انظري، يا أُخَيّة / ثِقي، يا أُخَيّة). Also 'Behold' is 'look/see', not تأمّل ('contemplate').
'Have faith' is religious in this cult context (Faith = الإيمان, frozen). ثِقي is secular 'trust me'.
تلهث = pants/breathes hard. Here the gasp is a shock reaction, immediately followed by 'I've... seen something terrible.'

Unresolved addressee, content-based only. Three lines in this node are unambiguously the male servant speaking to Genessa ('Twas my father's father who first served you', 'I… I am your humble servant' = masculine خادم). If 'You serve her?' is Genessa asking that servant - the reading that fits her not recognising the 'High Sester' title she queries in the same node - the verb must be masculine أتخدمُها. If instead the servant asks it of her, the current feminine form is right. No order data exists for this node (hash-tailed keys), so this needs a source check, not a blind fix.

In the _Stray variant this fragment is the broken restart of the same aphorism the two preceding rows carry ('Just as every flame casts a shadow' = كما تُلقي كل شعلة ظلًّا). فقط ('only') breaks that echo.
English 'I do' is an auxiliary contradiction ('you don't have to' -> 'I do [have to]'), not the lexical verb 'do'. بل أفعل reads as 'on the contrary, I perform [it]' and loses the obligation.
